semantics: Every listed TLSU operation is an architectural memory operation in the same TSO domain as scalar load/store.
TLSU memory operations participate in aq/rl/fence ordering and must not violate store->store ordering.
Except for each MGATHER_CAS lane read-modify-write, a TLSU memory operation may decompose into multiple internal beats and is architecturally non-atomic to external observers.
Internal beats have implementation-defined issue order; software must not infer row or element beat order from one architectural operation.
Page and access faults are precise and restartable by software.
TPREFETCH performs the same reads, address translation, permission checks, faults, restart, beat decomposition, coherence, and ordering as TLOAD, but allocates and writes no destination tile state.
MGATHER forms lane addresses from the base scalar and unsigned u16/u32/u64 offset-tile elements.
MSCATTER uses the same address formation and writes the corresponding data-tile elements.
MGATHER_MASK and MSCATTER_MASK suppress memory effects for masked-off lanes.
Each active MGATHER_CAS lane is one atomic read-modify-write that returns the observed value and conditionally stores the replacement value.
GMOV is the TLSU Function 13 core4 collective global-memory movement operation.

tso_axioms: Program-order store->store ordering is preserved for all addresses.
A younger load may read from memory before an older unrelated store becomes globally visible (store buffer behavior).
Store->load reordering is only visible as allowed by TSO; fence/aq/rl tighten ordering.
No operation may observe a younger store from the same LXCPU before an older store.
